name: Naga
summary: Along shores across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, Naga press toward the surface. Once the Highborne elite of the Kaldorei Empire, they were changed in the Great Sundering and now serve their ancient empress, Queen Azshara, beneath the sea.

sections.title: Fall of the Highborne
sections.body:
Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne ruled the Kaldorei Empire from Zin-Azshari. Queen Azshara and her inner court drew on the Well of Eternity, consumed by arcane power, to summon the Dark Titan Sargeras. Their act brought the invasion called the War of the Ancients. Then the Well collapsed and the Great Sundering began. The palace sank into the crushing abyss.

Facing annihilation, Azshara bargained with the Old Gods below. They spared her and her followers, changing them into cold, scaly serpentine beings bound to the deep.

sections.title: Depths of Nazjatar
sections.body: Beneath the Maelstrom, the survivors built the underwater empire of Nazjatar. For ten thousand years, the naga kept their Highborne arrogance and their grudge against the surface world. They became distinct casts: hulking warriors and sea witches with many arms, who weave spells. Under Azshara's gaze, they mastered sea creatures, storm magic, and frost sorcery. Their strength grew as they waited for a chance to strike at those who lived on land.

sections.title: The Resurfacing
sections.body:
The naga broke their silence during the Third War. Thrall's Horde first met the sea witch Zar'jira in the Great Sea. Lady Vashj answered Illidan Stormrage's summons and led naga forces through Dalaran's ruins.

Now naga camps press against coasts in Azshara, Darkshore, Ashenvale, Desolace, Feralas, Dustwallow Marsh, Hillsbrad, Arathi, and Stranglethorn. Ancient contempt and whispers of the Old Gods drive them to forge quiet alliances with the Twilight's Hammer and savage satyrs. They seek to claim what was once theirs.

faq.q: What were the naga before they were transformed?
faq.answer: The naga were once the Highborne, the aristocratic upper class of the ancient night elven empire. During the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago, the Well of Eternity collapsed and Queen Azshara and her courtiers drowned in the sea. The Old Gods offered salvation and changed them into serpentine aquatic beings.

Queen Azshara, the former empress of the Kaldorei, rules the naga. From Nazjatar beneath the Maelstrom, she directs her sea witches and warriors. The naga venerate her with fanatical devotion, even after thousands of years in monstrous forms.

faq.q: Why are naga attacking the beaches and coasts now?
faq.answer: The naga resurfaced during the Third War after hiding beneath the waves for ten thousand years. They believe ancient Kalimdor belongs to them as heirs of the Kaldorei Empire. Guided by Queen Azshara and the Old Gods, they seek to subjugate coastal lands and conquer the surface races.

faq.q: Why do male and female naga look so different?
faq.answer: Naga females retain the intellectual and magical cunning of their Highborne ancestors. Many have four arms and great skill with arcane, frost, and storm magic. Males are larger, hulking brutes with heavy scales and fins, shaped for physical warfare and violence.

faq.q: What is the relationship between the naga and Illidan Stormrage?
faq.answer: After the Third War, Illidan summoned allies from the deep sea with powerful magic. Lady Vashj answered with an army of naga, honoring ancient Highborne ties. Naga forces aided Illidan in the Broken Isles, Lordaeron, and beyond.

faq.q: Where can naga be encountered right now?
faq.answer: Naga hold beachheads along many coasts. In Kalimdor, they are numerous in Azshara, Darkshore, Ashenvale, Desolace, Feralas, and Dustwallow Marsh. In the Eastern Kingdoms, their raiding parties and altars can be found along the shores of Hillsbrad Foothills, Arathi Highlands, and Stranglethorn Vale.

angles.text: To the night elves, the naga are a painful reminder of the Highborne pride that shattered Ancient Kalimdor. Seeing Azshara's former court on the shores of Darkshore and Ashenvale makes them want to purge their ancient kin.

The Darkspear trolls hate the naga because the sea witch Zar'jira drove them from their island home during their voyage across the Great Sea. The attack claimed the life of their elder leader, Sen'jin.
The Alliance remembers the naga in Dalaran's ruins, where Lady Vashj's creatures captured survivors and stirred division between the blood elves and Grand Marshal Garithos's forces.
Thrall and the Horde fought naga raiders from the Darkspear Isles to Dustwallow Marsh. There, Lady Darkscale butchered human settlements and attacked the outskirts of Durotar.
